producer_report.summary: Gate and admission now share one rule. If a commit changes crates/athena-data/, both skip parsing athena.toml and defaults.toml with the running schema, because the candidate's own test in crates/athena-data/tests/repo_config.rs judges them. Otherwise they parse with the running schema. The host build of candidate code (check_with_candidate_schema, CHECK_MAIN) is removed from admission. A design note in docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md and a CHANGELOG entry record the decision and the alternatives. This send-back only re-ran the tests; I made no new edits. I did not re-read the design note or CHANGELOG this round. The full `cargo test --locked` returned without an error, but its output was too long for me to read the per-crate totals. I did not re-run fmt or clippy.

checks_run.note: Ran to completion with no error reported. The output was too long to read the totals.
The two gate tests matching 'schema' and the five athena-data unit tests passed.

criteria_check.criterion: Gate regression test: a commit that adds an athena.toml section and the matching athena-data schema change in one commit produces no Configuration violation from athena-gate content::check, while the same athena.toml change without a schema change is still refused with the parse error. Run: cargo test -p athena-gate.
criteria_check.evidence: In crates/athena-gate/src/content.rs, content::tests::a_new_section_with_its_schema_change_in_one_commit_is_not_refused passed. The existing a_configuration_that_does_not_parse_is_refused covers the same change without a schema change. deleting_the_schema_does_not_defer_the_parse also passed. I ran the first and last by name; the middle one was part of the full run, which showed no error.

criteria_check.criterion: Admission test: a candidate changing both crates/athena-data/ and athena.toml is admitted without any process being spawned to build candidate code, and an unknown section with no schema change is still a violation. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria_check.evidence: In crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs, the tests a_new_section_and_its_schema_change_together_are_admitted_without_a_build and an_unknown_section_without_a_schema_change_is_still_refused exist. The second passed in the earlier run (visible in the output); the first was part of the full run, which showed no error. Admission no longer has any code that spawns a build.

criteria_check.criterion: admission.rs no longer contains check_with_candidate_schema, CHECK_MAIN, or any Command::new(cargo) use on candidate files; grep shows none in athena-core or athena-gate.
criteria_check.evidence: A Grep for check_with_candidate_schema, CHECK_MAIN and Command::new over crates/ found no such names in admission.rs. The only Command::new calls in athena-core and athena-gate run git, gh, curl, a configured check program (checks.rs) and the secrets scanner binary (secrets.rs). None runs cargo on candidate files.

criteria_check.criterion: A test in crates/athena-data parses the repository's athena.toml and defaults.toml with that crate's own schema and fails if either does not parse, so a candidate's sandboxed cargo test judges its own schema. Run: cargo test -p athena-data.
criteria_check.evidence: cargo test --locked -p athena-data --test repo_config: athena_toml_parses_with_this_crates_schema, defaults_toml_parses_with_this_crates_schema and an_unknown_section_is_what_the_test_would_catch passed.

criteria_check.criterion: Both checks use one shared rule for deciding when to defer to the sandboxed test, so gate and admission cannot diverge. Run: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt --check all pass.
criteria_check.evidence: The shared rule is in crates/athena-data/src/lib.rs, with both checks calling it. cargo test --locked completed with no error. I did not re-run clippy or fmt in this send-back round, so the evidence for those is the earlier round.

criteria_check.criterion: A short design note records the decision with alternatives (host build, sandbox build, lenient parse) and states why candidate code is never built on the host; CHANGELOG notes the change.
criteria_check.evidence: The note is in docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md and the entry is in CHANGELOG.md. I wrote both earlier and did not re-read them this round.

mistakes: The first report did not list the criteria_check entries in the form required, which caused the send-back.
learnings: The Bash tool here cannot pipe and cannot run grep, so long cargo output has to be narrowed with test-name filters.
